itineraries.title: Cool Galleries by Day, Free Music by Night — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: Beat a 99°F Thursday indoors at the art museum, then ease into a free downtown concert after sundown
itineraries.drive_time: All within ~15 min of downtown Raleigh; NCMA to Moore Square is about 12 min
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$45 (tours free; spend is dinner + optional beach-music ticket)
itineraries.overview: It hits 99°F today, so bank the hot hours in the air-conditioned NC Museum of Art — a free docent tour, then the free NCMA After Hours as the galleries stay open late. When the sun drops, head downtown for the free Live After 5 concert at Moore Square, or swap in the North Hills beach-music series if you'd rather dance.

afternoon.title: Public Tour: The People's Collection
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh, NC 27607
afternoon.notes: Free 50-minute docent tour of the People's Collection — the museum's AC is the smartest place to be at 1 p.m. on a 99°F day.

evening.title: NCMA After Hours
evening.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh, NC 27607
evening.notes: NCMA After Hours: free general admission, art, and music as the galleries stay open into the evening.

evening.title: Live After 5: River Shook
evening.location: Moore Square, 201 S Blount St, Raleigh, NC 27601
evening.notes: Free Live After 5 concert with River Shook at Moore Square, with food trucks. Bring water.

evening.title: Too Much Sylvia — Midtown Beach Music Series
evening.location: Midtown Park at North Hills, 4011 Cardinal at North Hills St, Raleigh, NC 27609
evening.notes: Alternative: Too Much Sylvia at the North Hills beach-music series if you'd rather a shag-dancing lawn party (small ticket).

food.vegan_dish: Sunny Bowl with tofu, greens, and tahini
food.notes: Fast, cold, plant-forward — good fuel before the heat peaks.
Fully vegetarian/vegan on W Martin St; reserve ahead, then walk to Moore Square.

alternatives.good_weather: Free Live After 5 at Moore Square, or the open-air beach-music show at North Hills
alternatives.rain: Storms are unlikely tonight (Sunny), but if one pops up, the North Hills shops/restaurants and the museum galleries are steps away.

practical_notes: 99°F and humid — carry water and plan the museum for the hottest part of the afternoon.
NCMA has free parking; Moore Square has paid decks nearby on Blount and Wilmington.
Live After 5 is free and family-friendly; beer and wine are sold on-site.

itineraries.title: Third Friday 'Winter in July' + Bulls Fireworks — Durham
itineraries.theme: Durham's monthly downtown art walk (with a snow machine) paired with a Margaritaville night at the ballpark
itineraries.drive_time: Everything within ~10 min in downtown Durham; DBAP is a short walk from the art-walk district
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$40 (art walk + Foodie Fare free; Bulls ticket is the spend)
itineraries.overview: The hottest day of the week (100°F) is also the most fun after dark in Durham. Graze the Durham Foodie Fare food-truck market at Central Park, then hit the free Third Friday gallery crawl — July's edition is a 'Winter in July' party with a snow machine and a DJ. Cap it with Margaritaville Night and postgame fireworks at the Durham Bulls.

afternoon.title: Durham Foodie Fare
afternoon.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham, NC 27701
afternoon.notes: Durham Foodie Fare food-truck + art market at Durham Central Park — free entry, pay-as-you-go dinner.

evening.title: Third Friday Durham Art Walk & Gallery Crawl
evening.notes: Third Friday art walk across ~20 downtown galleries; the 'Winter in July' snow machine is a literal way to cool off.

evening.title: Third Friday Art Walk at Golden Belt
evening.location: Golden Belt Arts, 800 Taylor St, Durham, NC 27701
evening.notes: Stop into Golden Belt Arts for the studio art show and sale during the crawl.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs. Charlotte Knights — Margaritaville Night & Friday Night Fireworks
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham, NC 27701
evening.notes: Alternative evening: skip the crawl and do Margaritaville Night + Friday Night Fireworks at the Durham Bulls.

food.vegan_dish: Rotating vegan tacos or falafel from the truck lineup
food.notes: Free-entry market; menus vary by truck, so ask which are plant-based that night.

food.vegan_dish: Marinara pizza (no cheese) with roasted vegetables
food.notes: Sit-down alternative a block from the art walk if the trucks are packed.

alternatives.good_weather: Do both: art walk 6–8, then catch the Bulls fireworks
alternatives.rain: The art walk galleries are indoors and AC'd; the Bulls game may delay for weather, so check the gate before heading over.

practical_notes: 100°F — the art-walk galleries and the snow machine are your friends; hydrate.
Downtown Durham decks (Chapel Hill St, Church St) are the easiest parking for both the crawl and DBAP.
The art walk is free; Bulls tickets are separate and sell well on fireworks nights.

itineraries.title: Phish Night at Walnut Creek — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: A jam-band pilgrimage: amphitheater show plus a late-night afterparty downtown
itineraries.drive_time: Downtown Raleigh to Walnut Creek is ~15 min; afterparties are back downtown (~15 min)
itineraries.overview: Phish brings summer tour to the Coastal Credit Union Music Park at Walnut Creek. Fuel up with an early downtown dinner, catch the 7 p.m. show, then keep the night going at one of two official afterparties — Keller Williams at Lincoln Theatre or Kendall Street Company at The Pour House. It's a 100°F day, so pre-hydrate before the lawn.

evening.title: Phish
evening.location: Coastal Credit Union Music Park at Walnut Creek, 3801 Rock Quarry Rd, Raleigh, NC 27610
evening.notes: Phish at Walnut Creek — doors 5:30, show 7. Lawn seating bakes in the sun early; bring water and sunscreen.

evening.title: Keller Williams (Phish Afterparty - Late Show)
evening.location: Lincoln Theatre, 126 E Cabarrus St, Raleigh, NC 27601
evening.notes: Late show: Keller Williams' Phish afterparty at Lincoln Theatre downtown.

evening.title: Phish Afterparty: with Kendall Street Company
evening.location: The Pour House Music Hall & Record Shop, 224 S Blount St, Raleigh, NC 27601
evening.notes: Alternative afterparty: Kendall Street Company at The Pour House (cheaper cover).

food.vegan_dish: Vegan coconut curry with tofu and vegetables
food.notes: Laotian spot on Blount St; reserve, and eat by 5:30 to make the drive to Walnut Creek.
Plant-based comfort food if you want something hearty before a long night.

alternatives.good_weather: Lawn or reserved seats under open sky at Walnut Creek
alternatives.rain: Forecast is Sunny, but shows go on rain-or-shine; covered seating is limited, so pack a poncho just in case.

practical_notes: 100°F daytime — the lawn is exposed; hydrate before and during.
Walnut Creek parking backs up; leave downtown by 5:45 or rideshare.
Both afterparties start at 11:30 p.m. and run into the early morning — line up rides home.

itineraries.title: Farmers Market Morning to Night Market — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: A Saturday that opens at a morning farmers market and closes at a downtown twilight market, with the museum for the hot midday
itineraries.drive_time: North Hills to NCMA ~12 min; NCMA to Smoky Hollow ~12 min

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$40 (markets free to browse; spend is food + optional workshop)
itineraries.overview: Shop the Midtown Farmers' Market early while it's merely warm (it climbs to 98°F with afternoon storm chances), retreat to the NC Museum of Art for a free midday tour, then come back downtown for the free Raleigh Twilight Market at Smoky Hollow with 30+ vendors and a DJ once the heat breaks.

morning.title: Midtown Farmers' Market
morning.location: The Commons at North Hills, 4191 Main at North Hills St, Raleigh, NC 27609
morning.notes: Midtown Farmers' Market at North Hills — 35+ vendors; go early to beat the heat and the crowds.

afternoon.title: Summer Vendor Market at Compass Rose Brewery
afternoon.location: Compass Rose Brewery, 3201 Northside Dr, Raleigh, NC 27615
afternoon.notes: Air-conditioned browsing at the Compass Rose Brewery summer vendor market.

afternoon.title: Public Tour: The People's Collection
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh, NC 27607
afternoon.notes: Free docent tour at NCMA — the coolest way to spend the 98°F peak.

evening.title: Raleigh Twilight Market
evening.location: Smoky Hollow, 421 N Harrington St, Raleigh, NC 27603
evening.notes: Raleigh Twilight Market at Smoky Hollow — free evening market with local vendors, a DJ, and food/drinks.

food.vegan_dish: Fresh fruit + a vegan pastry from a market baker
food.notes: Graze the market for breakfast before the sun is high.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan chana masala / seasonal vegetable thali
food.notes: Indian-Asian on Martin St, a short walk from Smoky Hollow; strong veg menu.

alternatives.rain: Afternoon thunderstorms are possible — the NCMA galleries and the Compass Rose taproom are both indoor backups.

practical_notes: 98°F with afternoon storm chances — front-load the outdoor markets and keep the midday indoors.
North Hills and Smoky Hollow both have free/validated garage parking.
The Twilight Market is free; bring cash for vendors who don't take cards.

itineraries.title: Western Wake Family Saturday + International Rugby — Cary
itineraries.theme: A Cary day from the downtown farmers market to a makers market, capped by USA vs. Spain rugby at WakeMed
itineraries.drive_time: Downtown Cary to Fenton ~8 min; Fenton to WakeMed Soccer Park ~12 min

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$80 (markets + exhibit free; rugby ticket is the spend)
itineraries.overview: Spend a Cary Saturday close to the AC. Start at the Cary Downtown Farmers Market, cool off inside the free America the Revolution Experience exhibit at Downtown Cary Park, browse the Fenton Makers Market, then watch the USA Men's Eagles take on Spain in the World Rugby Nations Cup at WakeMed Soccer Park — the first international rugby there in a decade.

morning.title: Cary Downtown Farmers Market
morning.location: Cary Downtown Farmers Market, 160 E Park St, Cary, NC 27511
morning.notes: Cary Downtown Farmers Market — grower-only, open rain or shine; go early before 98°F.

afternoon.title: American Revolution Experience
afternoon.location: Gathering House at Downtown Cary Park, 327 S Academy St, Cary, NC 27511
afternoon.notes: Free, indoor America the Revolution Experience pop-up at the Gathering House — an AC break with interactive kiosks for kids.

afternoon.title: Fenton Makers Market
afternoon.notes: Fenton Makers Market — local makers at Cary's Fenton development, with plenty of indoor shops and restaurants.

evening.title: World Rugby Nations Cup: USA vs. Spain
evening.location: WakeMed Soccer Park, 101 Soccer Park Dr, Cary, NC 27511
evening.notes: World Rugby Nations Cup: USA vs. Spain at WakeMed Soccer Park — evening kickoff once it's cooled a bit.

food.vegan_dish: Impossible burger or a grain bowl from a Fenton eatery
food.notes: Fenton has AC and many options — an easy midday reset between markets.
Grab an early dinner in downtown Cary before heading to WakeMed.

alternatives.good_weather: Open-air seating at WakeMed Soccer Park
alternatives.rain: Afternoon storms are possible; the match is outdoors, so bring a poncho and check the gate policy.

practical_notes: 98°F — the indoor Revolution exhibit and Fenton's shops are good midday cool-downs.
Downtown Cary Park has a deck; WakeMed Soccer Park has on-site lots.
Rugby tickets vary by tier; buy ahead via the venue's ticketing link.

itineraries.title: Family Dino Day + Outdoor Movie — Raleigh & Wake Forest
itineraries.theme: An air-conditioned, kid-first Saturday of dinosaurs and farm fun, ending at a free outdoor movie once it cools
itineraries.drive_time: Downtown Raleigh to the Fairgrounds ~12 min; Raleigh to Joyner Park (Wake Forest) ~30 min

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $25–$70 for a family (Dino ticket + Marbles admission; movie is free)
itineraries.overview: A 98°F Saturday is a perfect day to stay indoors with the kids. Start at Marbles Kids Museum's Farm to Fork Kids Fest (seed-to-smoothie activities), roll over to the fully indoor Dinosaur Adventure at the Fairgrounds for animatronic dinos and fossil digs, then drive up to Wake Forest for a free outdoor screening of 'Mufasa: The Lion King' once the sun is down.

morning.title: Farm to Fork Kids Fest
morning.location: Marbles Kids Museum, 201 E Hargett St, Raleigh, NC 27601
morning.notes: Farm to Fork Kids Fest at Marbles — hands-on agriculture activities; included with admission.

afternoon.title: Dinosaur Adventure
afternoon.location: Kerr Scott Building, N.C. State Fairgrounds, 4285 Trinity Rd, Raleigh, NC 27607
afternoon.notes: Dinosaur Adventure at the Kerr Scott Building — fully indoor and AC'd, with rides, bounce houses, and fossil digs.

evening.title: Family Movie Nights at Joyner Park: Mufasa: The Lion King
evening.location: E. Carroll Joyner Park, 701 Harris Rd, Wake Forest, NC 27587
evening.notes: Free Family Movie Night at Joyner Park (Wake Forest): 'Mufasa' on a 32-ft inflatable screen, with a 7:30 pre-show for kids.

food.notes: Quick kid-friendly lunch between Marbles and the Fairgrounds.

food.vegan_dish: Veggie tacos or fries from an on-site truck
food.notes: Movie-night vendors sell snacks on site; bring a blanket.

alternatives.good_weather: Outdoor screening on the Joyner Park lawn
alternatives.rain: The movie may be canceled for rain — check the Town of Wake Forest page before driving up; the indoor Dino event can fill the afternoon either way.

practical_notes: 98°F — the museum and Dino exhibit are both indoor; save the outdoor movie for the evening.
Dinosaur Adventure and Marbles both charge admission; buy Dino tickets online to skip the line.
Joyner Park movie is free; arrive by 7:30 for the pre-show and a good lawn spot.

itineraries.title: Lazy Sunday: Broadway Matinee + Bulls Finale — Durham
itineraries.theme: A relaxed Durham Sunday from a games-and-beer afternoon to a matinee and the Bulls homestand finale
itineraries.drive_time: Everything within ~10 min in downtown Durham; the taproom, DPAC, and DBAP are all walkable

weather.summary: Chance Showers And Thunderstorms then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $15–$90 (games free; Notebook matinee + Bulls ticket are the spend)
itineraries.overview: Take Sunday slow in downtown Durham. Warm up with Dungeons & Drafts board games at The Glass Jug, catch the matinee of Broadway's 'The Notebook' at DPAC, then finish at the Durham Bulls' Community Hero Game with Kids Run the Bases. Storm chances are up (94°F), so this indoor-leaning plan has a weatherproof spine.

afternoon.title: Dungeons & Drafts
afternoon.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab (Downtown Durham), 545 Foster St Suite 10, Durham, NC 27701
afternoon.notes: Dungeons & Drafts tabletop gaming at The Glass Jug (downtown) — a cool, low-key start.

afternoon.title: The Notebook (Matinee)
afternoon.location: DPAC (Durham Performing Arts Center), 123 Vivian St, Durham, NC 27701
afternoon.notes: 'The Notebook' matinee at DPAC — indoor, AC'd, ~2h13m; a good rain plan.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs. Charlotte Knights — Community Hero Game & Kids Run the Bases
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham, NC 27701
evening.notes: Durham Bulls homestand finale vs. Charlotte, with Kids Run the Bases afterward.

food.vegetarian_dish: Vegetarian rice bowl with black beans
food.notes: Latin spot downtown with solid plant-based options, near DPAC.
Eat at the ballpark, or hit the adjacent American Tobacco Campus before first pitch.

alternatives.good_weather: Open-air seats at DBAP for the 5:05 finale
alternatives.rain: Afternoon/evening storms are likely (94°F) — the game may delay; the matinee and taproom keep the day dry regardless.

practical_notes: Storm chances today — this plan leans indoor, so it survives a washout.
Downtown Durham decks serve the taproom, DPAC, and DBAP; it's all walkable once parked.
The Notebook matinee and Bulls tickets are separate purchases; the game is the last home date until late July.

itineraries.title: Weeknight Out: Trivia, Bingo & Death Cab — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: A low-key Wednesday of brewery games and a marquee amphitheater show
itineraries.drive_time: Downtown/North Raleigh breweries ~15 min apart; Walnut Creek is ~15 min from downtown

weather.summary: Slight Chance Rain Showers then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$90 (brewery games free; Death Cab ticket + dinner are the spend)
itineraries.overview: Make a midweek night of it. Grab the Wednesday dinner special at Ponysaurus Raleigh, play free music bingo, or test your team at Compass Rose — then head to Walnut Creek for Death Cab for Cutie's 'I Built You a Tower' tour. It's 94°F with evening storm chances, so keep a poncho handy for the lawn.

afternoon.title: Wednesday Dinner at Ponysaurus Raleigh
afternoon.location: Ponysaurus Brewing Co. (Raleigh), 2221 Iron Works Dr, Raleigh, NC 27604
afternoon.notes: Wednesday dinner special (vodka chicken parm on house focaccia) at Ponysaurus Raleigh.

evening.title: Music Bingo Tuesdays at Ponysaurus Raleigh
evening.location: Ponysaurus Brewing Co. (Raleigh), 2221 Iron Works Dr, Raleigh, NC 27604
evening.notes: Free music bingo at Ponysaurus Raleigh if you're skipping the concert.

evening.title: Death Cab for Cutie: I Built You A Tower World Tour
evening.location: Coastal Credit Union Music Park at Walnut Creek, 3801 Rock Quarry Rd, Raleigh, NC 27610
evening.notes: Death Cab for Cutie at Walnut Creek — the marquee show of the night.

food.vegan_dish: Ask for the plant-based special or a side of focaccia + veggies
food.notes: Wednesday dinner special pairs with the taproom's beer; eat before the drive to Walnut Creek.
Warehouse District alternative if you want a sit-down meal downtown first.

alternatives.good_weather: Death Cab on the amphitheater lawn
alternatives.rain: Evening storms are possible (94°F) — if the show delays or you'd rather stay dry, the free Ponysaurus music bingo is an indoor Plan B.

practical_notes: 94°F with evening storm chances — pack a poncho for the Walnut Creek lawn.
Ponysaurus Raleigh (Iron Works Dr) has its own lot; Walnut Creek parking backs up, so leave early.
Music bingo and trivia are free; the Death Cab ticket is the night's real cost.
